chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A servant may make an exception within forty days if he forgets. Indeed, some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and asked him about certain matters. So he said to them, “Come tomorrow and I will inform you,” and he did not make an exception. Then Jibrīl عليه السلام was withheld from him for forty days. Then he came to him and said:
“And do not say about anything: Indeed I will do that tomorrow, except if Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ: forty, indicating the time limit mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.اذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ: remember your Lord, the Quranic instruction upon forgetting
key_terms.الْيَهُودِ: the Jews who came and asked questions
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrīl, the angel who brought revelation
key_terms.نَسِيَ: forgot, referring to omission out of forgetfulness
key_terms.يَسْتَثْنِيَ: to make an exception by saying 'if Allah wills'
key_terms.يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ: if Allah wills, expressing dependence on the divine will

ai.seo_question: Can someone say “if Allah wills” later if they forgot to say it initially?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that if a person forgets to say “if Allah wills,” he may still add the exception within forty days. It supports this ruling by citing the event in which Jibrīl عليه السلام was delayed after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said he would answer the next day without saying “if Allah wills,” followed by the revelation of the Quranic instruction.
